Hi guys. I just want to add one more comment how this change is breaking a lot of deployments. 
Currently we are using mysql_db module for dump and import. So we are dumping one database and importing it to another. If the dumped file now has a ``USE` `db_name`;`` statement, the import module will ignore the database name and it will import the db to the name in this `USE` statement. So back to itself.  

This doesn't work any more:
```
- name: Dump the database
  mysql_db:
    state: dump
    name: database1
    login_user: "{{ db_user }}"
    login_host: "{{ db_host }}"
    login_password: "{{ db_pass }}"
    single_transaction: yes
    target: "{{ dump_file }}"

- name: Import the database
  mysql_db:
    state: import
    name: database2
    login_user: "{{ db_user }}"
    login_host: "{{ db_host }}"
    login_password: "{{ db_pass }}"
    target: "{{ dump_file }}"
  register: dbimport_try
  retries: 3
  delay: 5
  until: dbimport_try is not failed

```
With this bug, import to databse2 will never be executed. 
I think the best way would be to revert and not use `USE` statement in dumps. Otherwise you would have to delete this part from dump somehow before every import. Or use option in the dump module to mitigate this. 

Nice regards,
Marko

We encountered the same issue. IMO Ansible should not use `--databases` unless multiple databases are specified (this is the pre-Ansible-2.9 behavior). Maybe add an option to control the use of `--databases`. Adding `--no-create-db` as an option would not fix this as the dump would still contain a `USE` statement.

This is our workaround for now:

```yaml
# https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/65351
- name: WORKAROUND - Remove "CREATE DATABASE" and "USE" statements from SQL dump
  command: sed -i -e '/^CREATE DATABASE /d' -e '/^USE /d' /tmp/dump.sql
```
Lets not forget about this please! It broke one of our tasks and we will have to apply the fix @fnkr mentioned.  It also took us days to even figure out this is what did it.

@Andersson007 `--no-create-db` does not fix this. The option suppresses the `CREATE DATABASE` statement, but it does not suppress the `USE` statement. Each of these statements causes the import to fail. `--databases` must not be used for single-database dumps, otherwise it will break if source and target database name differ.

This is the commit that introduced this bug: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/44058e942588425197208ce7976559d9a49b86d1#diff-4eeda2d2fc550548c262c40b0fbdb808R172

> --no-create-db does not fix this

Though it should do the job with `dump_extra_args: --tables` (no arguments). It's a bit of a hack (https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mysqldump/):

> This option overrides the --databases (-B) option. mysqldump regards all name arguments following the option as table names.
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/67767 should work. Could anyone please try
